thread:
inc-bot: ALERT: elevated 5xx rate for tool_calling endpoints in eu-north-1 and ap-south-1 :rotating_light:
pagerduty-bot: Paging Dmitri (oncall) — escalation level 1 :phone:
Dmitri (oncall): Ack. Pulling up traces and dashboards. Which customers reporting?
Marta (customer-success): Two customers pinged support: LedgerCo and Shoply. Both see failed tool-run calls and repeated client retries since ~02:04 UTC.
Asha (eng-runtime): Looking at runtime logs: repeatedly seeing error: "INCOMPATIBLE_VARIANT: missing_tool_shim_or_context_too_short". Router routed tool_calling traffic to redwood-v2-7b-quant-2 due to cost-pref policy.
Kenji (router): Hmm, router cache lists redwood-v2-7b-quant-2 as supports_tool_calling=true. But the runtime says otherwise. Sample routing trace: ```
[02:05:10] router select: req=r-882 policy=cost-pref chose=eu-north-1:node-7 model=redwood-v2-7b variant=quant-2 supports_tool_calling=true
[02:05:11] runtime: pop request -> ERROR INCOMPATIBLE_VARIANT (tool_call shim not present or context_limit < 4096)
[02:05:11] router: fallback to ap-south-1:node-3 model=redwood-v2-7b-fp16
[02:05:12] router: fallback back to eu-north-1 (no loop-breaker set)
```
Tess (sre): Looks like two issues: 1) compatibility metadata mismatch (quant variant incorrectly advertised), 2) router allowed immediate cross-region fallback without loop protection causing bounce and amplification.
Dmitri (oncall): Immediate mitigation suggestions: a) Add a quick policy override to exclude *quant* variants from tool_calling traffic. b) Enable fallback_count guard to prevent bouncing. c) Notify customers and reduce retry aggressiveness at edge. Who can push the override?
Kenji (router): I'll push override to policy-store: `POST /v1/overrides {"id":"block-quant-toolcall-1772222222","expr":"request.tool_calling == true -> exclude:quant"}`. Starting deploy.
deploy-bot: policy-store override deployment started (id=ov-4123)
Asha (eng-runtime): Also, I'll modify the runtime to emit an explicit header `X-Model-Compat: tool_calling=false` when the model variant can't run tool_calling. That will give router a defensive signal. Pushing small patch now.
Marta (customer-success): Sent initial message to LedgerCo and Shoply acknowledging the issue and that we're mitigating; they'll standby for confirmation.
deploy-bot: override deployed to primary in eu-north-1 at 02:08:34 UTC
Kenji (router): Forcing compatibility cache refresh across edge nodes: `POST /v1/cache/refresh {"keys":["model-compat"]}`. TTL was 60m; forcing immediate fetch.
Tess (sre): Adding fallback guard to router: if request.meta.fallback_count >= 1 then route to fallback-model group (fp16) and set retry_allowed=false. Pushing to canary in eu-north-1 now.
Asha (eng-runtime): Quick metric snapshot: 02:00-02:10 UTC pre-fix tool_calling 5xxs +380%. After override & guard (02:09-02:20) 5xxs down ~90%. Median latency tool calls down from 1.6s to 0.45s.
Marta (customer-success): LedgerCo confirms tool-run success at 02:10 UTC. Shoply reports normal behavior at 02:11 UTC.
Dmitri (oncall): Root cause hypothesis: model-catalog publish had stale/incorrect compatibility flags for quant variants (manual publish step omitted runtime shim flag). Router's hourly sync didn't pick up a recent correction due to a partial sync failure. Router then selected quant variant for tool_calling; runtime rejected; fallback policy without loop protection caused cross-region bounce and client retries amplified errors.
Kenji (router): Short-term corrective actions: 1) Keep override in place for 48h. 2) Reduce compatibility cache TTL to 5m. 3) Add immediate refresh webhook on model-catalog publish. 4) Add fallback_count guard (deployed to prod).
Asha (eng-runtime): Long-term fixes: 1) Authoritative compatibility API with strong consistency (gRPC/ETag) so router never trusts stale cached flags. 2) CI gating: any variant marked supports_tool_calling must pass a runtime shim check during publish. 3) Add e2e test that simulates tool_calling routing to ensure router+runtime compatibility.
Tess (sre): I'll open PRs for TTL reduction and loop-breaker enforcement and link them to the incident.
Dmitri (oncall): Postmortem owner: Asha (eng-runtime). Please produce timeline, exact customer impact (requests failed, percent error increase), and a proposed rollout plan for the authoritative API. Due EOD tomorrow.
Asha (eng-runtime): Acknowledged. I'll include logs and the compatibility excerpt for the postmortem: ```
compatibility snippet:
- redwood-v2-7b-fp16: supports_tool_calling: true
- redwood-v2-7b-quant-2: supports_tool_calling: false (runtime-level shim missing, context_limit=2048)
```
Marta (customer-success): I'll follow up with customers with a timeline and invite them to the postmortem.
Dmitri (oncall): Marking incident as mitigated. Will monitor for 2 hours. If we see regressions, page immediately. Thanks all for fast turnaround. :thumbsup:
inc-bot: INCIDENT STATUS UPDATE: P2 -> mitigated; metrics returning to baseline.
